list.title: Mapping profiles
list.heading: Mapping profiles
list.caption: Stored mapping profiles
list.name: Name
list.newHint: Choose a sample file carrying the header the mapping should apply to. The editor opens with your real columns and values.
list.importHint: An export from this importer is expected. If it carries no sample, the profile can only be edited once a matching table has been supplied.
list.updated: Existing profile “{name}” updated from the file.
list.importedNoSample: Profile “{name}” created. The file carried no sample — supply a matching table and the mapping becomes editable.
list.emptyText: Upload a sample file to create the first one.
list.footer: Profiles are visible to every institution. When a file with a known header is uploaded, your own profile wins; foreign ones are offered for adoption and copied in the process, so changes never alter anyone else's imports.

new.title: New mapping
new.heading: Create a mapping from a sample file
new.lead: The file is only read, never stored. What is kept are the column names and a few sample rows — enough for the preview to work on real values.
new.dropText: Drop a file here or click
new.footer: If the header is already known, no second profile is created: you are taken to the existing one, whose sample data is refreshed on the way.

detail.openColumns: nothing open | one column open | {n} columns open
detail.sampleHint: The editor calculates the preview on real rows. None are stored for this profile — that happens with profiles from an export without a sample. Upload the table the profile applies to; only column names and a few sample rows are kept.
detail.deleteText: Really delete this profile? The {n} imports already converted stay as they are; future uploads with this header will need a mapping again.
detail.foreignHint: This profile belongs to another institution. You can adopt it while mapping a file of your own — it is copied in the process.
detail.restoreText: Activate version {n} again? The current state stays in the history as an earlier version. Imports already converted are not re-run.

checkMsg.chain_date: “{field}” expects a date in ISO format. Add the converter “Date to ISO”?
checkMsg.chain_language: “{field}” expects an ISO 639-2 code. Add the converter “Language to ISO 639-2”?
checkMsg.authority_unsupported: “Look up authority data” has no effect on “{field}” — identifiers can only be attached to persons, subjects, places, genres and identifier targets.
checkMsg.enum_no_valuemap: “{field}” has a fixed list of values — without a mapping, deviating spellings are reported.
checkMsg.enum_empty_valuemap: The value list for “{field}” is still empty. As long as no target value is entered, nothing arrives for this column.
checkMsg.default_unknown_target: A fixed value points at a target that does not exist.
checkMsg.work_no_title: No column leads to “Work › Titles › Main title”. The title of the manifestation or item is used instead.
checkMsg.data_separator: The values contain a separator. “{field}” takes several values — with “Split” each value becomes its own entry instead of one long string.
checkMsg.value_truncated: “{field}” takes only one value; further values in this cell are left out.
checkMsg.chain_shorthand: A converter was stored as a plain string and has been turned into an object.
checkMsg.chain_unknown_op: An unknown converter has been removed.
checkMsg.authority_ambiguous: “{value}” matches {n} authority records. No ID was entered. Please assign it manually.
checkMsg.transform_notABoolean: “{wert}” is neither a yes nor a no
checkMsg.transform_badDate: “{wert}” could not be read as a date
checkMsg.transform_badDuration: “{wert}” could not be read as a duration
checkMsg.transform_notInValuemap: The value “{wert}” is not listed in the value mapping

checkMsg.target_identifierPattern: “{wert}” does not match the identifier pattern of “{ziel}”

checkMsg.target_badDate: “{wert}” is not a permitted date (expected YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD)

checkMsg.authority_limit: The limit of {grenze} authority lookups per import has been reached.
checkMsg.authority_unreachable: The authority source {quelle} was unreachable — no match was recorded.
checkMsg.export_foreign: The file does not come from this importer. It is being read on a trial basis.
checkMsg.identifier_duplicate: The identifier “{id}” already appears in row {zeile}. Two objects with the same identifier fail the schema check. Either the rows mean the same object — in which case work grouping should be configured accordingly — or the column is unsuitable as an identifier and should be mapped to a different target.
